description: Mobile-phone photograph (screenshot with black letterbox bars) of the Bangkok skyline under hazy skies. The central subject is the King Power MahaNakhon skyscraper, recognizable by its distinctive spiral pixelated cutout facade; in the foreground stands a white building lettered ASSUMPTION COLLEGE, a school in Bangrak, Bangkok, flanked by other high-rise towers.

Screenshot of the top of an official U.S. Department of Justice (District of Nevada) organizational chart for the Infraud Organization cybercrime ring, with DOJ, HSI Las Vegas, and Henderson PD seals. A headline line states 13 criminals from 17 countries were arrested for defrauding victims of over $530 million with over $2.2 billion in losses. The chart shows silhouette placeholders for Defendant #1 Svyatoslav Bondarenko aka Obnon (Administrator) and Defendant #2 Sergei Medvedev aka Stells (Administrator), the latter stamped APPREHENDED, with more silhouettes cropped below.

description: Meme collage titled 'WHEN YOU HAVE CONCENTRATION CAMPS' with heart-eyes emoji, criticizing U.S. media coverage of North Korea at the February 2018 Winter Olympics as fawning. It combines Pepe the Frog cartoons in communist military garb, a 'Commie News Network' parody of the CNN logo, and screenshots of real coverage: a CNN tweet on Kim Jong Un's sister Kim Yo Jong 'stealing the show', a CNN article 'North Korea is winning the Olympics', a Michael Moore tweet praising the opening ceremony, plus New Yorker, NBC Olympics, Wall Street Journal, ThinkProgress and Esquire items on the North Korean cheer squad. A caption block accuses the media of siding with slavery and death camps out of hatred of Pence and the Trump administration.

description: Screenshot of a two-column list of 65 numbered passenger names plus 6 crew members, in awkward machine-translated English (e.g. surname-first entries, 'child' notations, and garbled lines like 'THE WILDLIFE Anatoly' and 'SON OF ULYAN'). A header instructs: 'We need to identify a person on this list that was associated with the dossier and/or uranium one.' A hand-drawn red arrow points to entry #32. Context and the archive filename ('Russian Plane crash list') indicate this is a translated passenger manifest circulated after the 11 February 2018 Saratov Airlines Flight 703 crash near Moscow, used to hunt for a passenger allegedly tied to the Steele dossier or Uranium One.
text: We need to identify a person on this list that was associated with the dossier and/or uranium one. [65 numbered passenger names and a 6-name crew list follow — victims' names withheld as private individuals; two child passengers are marked '(child)']. Also, a list of crew members:
flags: Names withheld: list consists of private individuals (plane-crash victims), including minors
Red arrow singles out passenger #32, named in the list as Ivanov Vyacheslav — a private individual; the implied dossier/Uranium One connection is an unverified crowd-sourced claim
Flight identification inferred from filename and context, not stated in the image

description: Screenshot of a verified tweet by writer Raza Ahmad Rumi (@Razarumi), dated 11 February 2018, paying tribute to Pakistani human-rights lawyer Asma Jahangir following her death. It praises her for speaking truth to power and defending the downtrodden. Attached are two black-and-white photographs of Jahangir at protests: one shows her speaking forcefully in front of a line of helmeted riot police, the other shows women, one identified by context as Jahangir, being restrained by police in a street crowd.
text: Raza Ahmad Rumi @Razarumi. Follow. 'Speaking truth to power' a phrase, we often use. #AsmaJahangir lived,practiced till her last breath.
